title: Scripts maintainability: internal typed tooling and thin commands
summary: Audit of eight maintained scripts (1090 lines): all retain a current caller or documented reproduction purpose. The authorized follow-up moves reusable Node code into an internal TypeScript/ES-module library with thin commands and named Python operations. Visual-review replay now retains saved errors and inventory bytes, and renderer reporting distinguishes planar views from spatial 3D. No standalone package is justified by the inspected consumers.
decision_provenance: The user requested an audit of usefulness, simplification, library placement and the JavaScript stack, then asked the assistant to use its judgment with maintainability as the goal. The architecture and migration sequence below are assistant recommendations. This audit did not implement a code or dependency migration. The user subsequently authorized implementation with "sounds good, go fix"; that follow-up is recorded separately below.
findings: Four files are command/build entry points and four are reusable modules. Reference discovery establishes maintained use, not invocation frequency.
task_visual_review.cjs --from-inventory replaces prior summary.errors with an empty list, rewrites the source name and returns status 0. Reproduced with a synthetic failed inventory and no browser.
task_visual_review.cjs treats every non-static view as spatial 3D, while use-scene-player.ts supports planar DOM/SVG story rendering. This is a code-inspection finding, not a fresh rendering result.

export_med_tours.cjs mixes parsing, configuration, timing, captions, browser lifecycle, encoding and output writes in a 323-line entry point. The existing encoder and composed-capture helpers already have useful boundaries.
Current TypeScript coverage includes zero scripts and zero JavaScript tests. The optional Python anatomy recipe also sits outside routine Python style gates, although its direct Ruff checks pass.
The staged frontend builder already uses Python-owned input discovery. Build and story export still hard-code .venv/bin/python and embed Python source snippets.
The anatomy builder remains a documented, source-hash-pinned optional reproduction recipe. Its heavy imaging dependencies and fixed-case policy should remain outside the default library.
recommendations: Fix inventory replay and planar classification before module-format changes.
Keep thin commands in scripts and ordinary internal TypeScript/ES-module helpers under presentation/tooling, with one existing root package manifest.

Add strict Node tooling checks and declared Node types; migrate direct consumers together. Keep frontend bundler resolution separate. Account explicitly for the declared Node 22.13 floor when selecting native TypeScript execution.
Extract typed tour configuration/timing/caption planning and explicit export operations. Use built-in argument parsing. Preserve encoder cleanup and exact composed-frame capture.
Expose named operations in the existing Python owners instead of embedded Python snippets. Keep canonical records, source fingerprints and story compilation in Python.
Update build and story-batch fingerprint lists when relocating code. Preserve historical receipts and original outcomes.

Reconsider a standalone package only after a second application needs a stable, workspace-independent API. Defer replacing the shared browser harness with a test framework until it removes demonstrated maintenance work.
